key_insight: Model the physical world as a collection of actionable objects — each object carries an internal, learnable representation of state + affordances — so world models can predict how objects will respond to actions compositionally and generalize across novel interactions.
problem_solved: Existing world models often treat scenes holistically or statically, failing to capture object-level affordances and action-conditioned dynamics needed for robust planning, transfer, and interaction in physical environments.
method: Object-centric representation: factor scene into object tokens that encode state and actionable affordances.
Action-conditioned dynamics: a module predicts object responses and inter-object effects given candidate actions, enabling compositional rollouts.
Learning objectives: train on multi-modal interaction data (sim + real) with contrastive/behavioral losses to align affordances with usable actions and improve generalization.
impact: Provides a compact, interpretable substrate for planning and control — improving sample efficiency, transfer to novel tasks/objects, and downstream robotics/embodied-AI applications by making world models actionable and compositional.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: scene → object decomposition → object tokens with affordances → action-conditioned rollout → predicted outcome
Before/after sequences: short video frames or image pairs showing how different actions change object states
Affordance icons/overlays: per-object icons indicating graspable/pushable/rotatable affordances
Embedding map: 2D visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP) of object tokens colored by affordance or controllability
paper_authors: Kunqi Xu, Jitao Li, Jianglong Ye, Tianshu Tang, Isabella Liu
